95a36787-89ac-4e4f-ac50-60708ab61363#111.source:
Returns the WHANDLE of a client window from the parent window's WHANDLE.

```foxpro
SYS(2325, nWHANDLE)
```

**nWHANDLE**
Specifies an integer WHANDLE to a FoxPro window. A WHANDLE is an internal Visual FoxPro structure (represented by an integer) that is a wrapper around an inner client window's hWnd.

Numeric.

SYS(2325) returns the WHANDLE (internal VFP window handle) for a client window (WCLIENTWINDOW) of a specified Visual FoxPro parent window. nWHANDLE is returned if nWHANDLE is valid but there is no WCLIENTWINDOW. 0 is returned if nWHANDLE is invalid.

This function is intended for use with routines in the Visual FoxPro API Library Construction Kit. See the API Library Construction topic for more information about creating API libraries.

In Visual FoxPro 9.0, BINDEVENT( ) supports binding to Window Message (Win Msg) events. BINDEVENT( ) catches events passed to a hWnd (Window Handle). Many Visual FoxPro windows have an inner client window of type WCLIENTWINDOW which has its own hWnd. SYS(2325) lets you determine the WHANDLE of an inner client window.

SYS(2327) and SYS(2326) can be used to convert between a hWnd (Window Handle) and a Visual FoxPro WHANDLE.

- AEVENTS( ) Function
- BINDEVENT( ) Function
- SYS(2326) - WHANDLE from a Window's hWnd
- SYS(2327) - Window's hWnd from Visual FoxPro WHANDLE
- UNBINDEVENTS( ) Function

95ac342d-40cf-446d-b053-a40358985825#111.source:
You can use a wizard to help you create a database table, or you can create an empty database table. A wizard helps you create a table using your answers to a series of questions.

> **Note:** When you create a database table with an open database, the database table is associated automatically with the open database. If multiple databases are open, the table is associated with the open database set as the current database. The table's association with the database is stored as a back link in the table's header record. For more information, see Databases in Visual FoxPro and How to: Open Databases .

When you create a table, a table (.dbf) file is created to store the table file. For information about naming tables, see How to: Name Tables.

- Open the database you want to create a table in.
- On the Database menu, click Create Table .
- In the New Table dialog box, click Table Wizard .
- Follow the instructions on the wizard screens.

For more information, see Table Wizard.

You can also begin the wizard from a project in the Project Manager by expanding the Data node, the Databases node, and then node for your database. Click the Tables node, and then New. In the New Table dialog box, click Table Wizard. For more information, see Project Manager Window.

- Open the database you want to create a table in.
- On the Database menu, click Create Table .
- In the New Table dialog box, click New Table .
- In the Create dialog box, select the location you want to save the database table, and type a name for the table.
- Click Save . The Table Designer opens so you can specify table fields, items, and other attributes.

For more information, see Table Designer (Visual FoxPro).

- Open the project with the database in the Project Manager .
- In the Project Manager , expand the Data node, the Databases node, and then node for your database.
- Click the Tables node, New , and then New Table .
- In the Create dialog box, select the location you want to save the database table, and type a name for the table.
- Click Save . The Table Designer opens so you can specify table fields, items, and other attributes.

For more information, see Project Manager Window and Table Designer (Visual FoxPro).

- Open the database you want to create a table for.
- Perform one of the following: To create a table by opening the Table Designer , use the CREATE command. -OR- To create a table without opening the Table Designer , use the SQL CREATE TABLE command.

For more information, see CREATE Command and CREATE TABLE - SQL Command.

- How to: Edit Table Structure
- Working with Tables (Visual FoxPro)
- Creating Tables

964140ac-f3df-40c8-86e2-92e44c51027b#111.source: You can activate or disable IntelliSense functionality using the IntelliSense Manager or programmatically. By default, IntelliSense functionality is activated.

- On the Tools menu, click IntelliSense Manager .
- In the IntelliSense Manager dialog box, click the General tab.
- To disable IntelliSense, clear the Enable IntelliSense check box. -OR- To activate IntelliSense, select the Enable IntelliSense check box.

You can also activate or disable IntelliSense functionality programmatically by setting the appropriate values in the EditorOptions property using the _VFP system variable. For more information, see Visual FoxPro IntelliSense Manager Window and EditorOptions Property.

You can also set levels of availability for different parts of IntelliSense functionality. For example, when IntelliSense is set to Manual, you can activate IntelliSense using keyboard shortcuts. For more information, see How to: Set IntelliSense Options.

968fa1c6-2111-44f0-8111-e2f9f4b9fa57#111.source:
You have attempted to select a table outside the 32K work area range or are attempting to reference a file variable in a table that is not open. This error can occur under the following conditions:
 - A table or cursor that is specified for the RowSource property of a ComboBox or ListBox control is closed. If you want to close a table or cursor that is specified for the RowSource property of a ComboBox or ListBox control, perform either of the following actions prior to closing the table or cursor: Set the RowSource property to an empty value (""). -OR- Release the form containing the ComboBox or ListBox control.
- A SQL SELECT statement that recreates a table or cursor that is specified by the RowSource property is issued. When the SQL SELECT statement executes, Visual FoxPro closes then opens the table. To avoid this error, set the RowSource property to an empty value (""), issue the SQL SELECT statement, and reset the RowSource property to its previous value.

The report builder application, reportbuilder.app, features an Options dialog box where various configuration settings can be adjusted.

> **Important:** Unlike the settings in the Visual FoxPro Options Dialog Box (Visual FoxPro) , adjustments to report builder settings in this dialog box do not persist between Visual FoxPro sessions.

> **Tip:** You can remove access to this dialog box for end-users modifying reports, by issuing the MODIFY REPORT | LABEL command with the PROTECTED keyword in your application.

- Right-click the report layout background, and select Properties… from the context menu. - OR - Open the Properties dialog box of any report control or report band.
- Right-click the surface of the dialog box to display the dialog boxes context menu.
- Select Options… The Builder Options dialog box appears.

- Report Builder Options Dialog Box (Report Builder)
- Extending Reports at Design Time

970e4fb1-9418-4433-8d49-27fb835c76e1#112.source:
Allows you to customize the behavior of Component Gallery folders.

This dialog appears when you click Properties on the shortcut menu of a selected folder.

Enables specifying settings that are global for all catalogs. The following settings are available in this tab:
 **Name**
Displays the value in the Text field as the component label in the Component Gallery .
**Description**
Optional information from the Desc field that displays in the description pane of the Component Gallery .
**Picture**
Value in the Folderpict field that specifies the path and file name of the graphic used to represent the selected item in the gallery.
**Item picture**
Value in the Picture field which specifies the path and file name of the graphic used to represent items in this catalog that have no specified picture.
**Item desc**
Value in the Typedesc field which contains a description that applies to all items contained in this catalog or folder.

A node is any selectable gallery item. Enables specifying settings that are global for all catalogs. The following settings are available in this tab:
 **ID**
The name of the table plus the value in the ID field for the selected folder.
**Link ID**
If the selected item is a link, specifies the name of the source item.
**Classname**
The value in the Classname field which specifies the name of the class of the selected folder.
**Class library**
The value in the Classlib field which specifies the name and path to the class library containing the gallery item.
**Itemclass**
The value in the Itemclass field which specifies the default class of items in the selected folder that have no previously assigned class.
**Dynamic folder**
Value in the Filename field which contains the target expression, filename, or URL that is launched when you select this dynamic folder item.

This tab provides a place to specify events or properties that are global for all folders. The following areas are available in this tab:
 **Script**
The value in the Script field which contains any event script related to this catalog and its items.
**Properties**
The value in the Properties field which can contain value assignments to properties of the item.

Enables specifying settings that are global for all catalogs. The following settings are available in this tab:
 **Comments**
The value in the Comment field which contains user comments about usage, characteristics, or anything.
**User**
The value in the User field which contains user comments about usage, characteristics, or anything.
